---
name: recall
description: Show what DD knows on a topic when the user asks.
---

# Recall DD knowledge

Run `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/src/cli.js" recall "<what to look up>"` from the project and relay the
memories it prints. DD already delivers memories when the work touches what they cover; use this only for
an explicit question.

---
name: review
description: Open DD's review UI for candidates and stale memories.
---

# Review DD knowledge

Run `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/src/cli.js" doctor` from the project first and tell the user its
`summary` line, with the `problems` it lists, if any. Then run `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/src/cli.js" ui`
from the project, in the background, and show the user the address it prints, on its own line and exactly
as printed: the `?key=` part is what lets the browser in. Candidates, stale memories, agent requests and
trigger health are reviewed there by a person.

---
name: save
description: Save project knowledge an agent could not get from the code, when the user asks or a fix taught it.
---

# Save project knowledge

With the Write tool (on Codex, `apply_patch`), create one JSON file per memory in `.dd/inbox/` (any name
ending in `.json`; a file made through a shell command is not read). DD validates it at once and answers in the same turn: stored
(as a candidate, or active when DD verified its evidence), or rejected with reasons; fix the file and
write it again.

Fields: `topic` (two to four lowercase segments, `area/subject`), `kind` (`decision`, `trap`,
`failed_approach`, `fact` or `procedure`), `title`, `body` (what to do and why, naming the files, symbols,
commands or values it is about; at most 1,500 characters), `not_derivable` (one line: why reading the
code, tests and docs would not reveal this), `triggers` (clauses such as
`{ "on": ["edit"], "paths": ["src/store/*.js"], "symbols": ["openStore"] }`) and `evidence`: a repository
file `{ "type": "file", "path": "src/x.js" }`, an id DD gave you `{ "type": "observation", "ref": "e1a2b3c4" }`
or `{ "type": "correction", "ref": "..." }`, or `{ "type": "note", "summary": "..." }`. Without triggers,
DD uses the ones it suggested for the fix you cite. When the user asked to save it, add
`"origin": "user_explicit"`. Save only what changes what a capable agent would do.

To ask for a change to an existing memory instead, write `{ "request": "archive" | "revise" |
"reverify" | "merge" | "delete", "target": "<id or topic>", "why": "..." }`; it waits for a person in
the review UI. `reverify` re-hashes stale evidence once you checked the claim still holds; `merge` also
names `"into": "<id or topic>"`, the memory that keeps the knowledge (revise it first if it must say
more); `delete` takes ids of archived or superseded memories only. Archive, reverify and delete accept a
list of up to 200 targets.

When you save or request several things at once, give them one `"batch": "<name>"` (letters, digits,
`-` or `_`, at most 64 characters, for example the task's name): the person accepts or rejects the
whole lot in one action in the review UI. Each item is still validated on its own; one that is refused
is reported and the others go through.

# DeltaDictum [![CI](https://github.com/CribbNicolas/deltadictum/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/CribbNicolas/deltadictum/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/deltadictum)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/deltadictum) [![node](https://img.shields.io/node/v/deltadictum)](package.json) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Shield%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE) DeltaDictum (DD) gives a coding agent the engineering knowledge your code does not show, right before it acts: the decisions behind the code, the traps someone already fell into, the steps nothing enforces. Each memory says when it applies, what to do, and why the code alone would not tell the agent. DD delivers it when the agent reads, edits or runs something the memory covers, once per session, and stays silent otherwise. Memories are JSON files in your repository, shared through git; everything else stays on your machine. No account, no model calls, no background process, no dependencies. **Documentation: [cribbnicolas.github.io/deltadictum](https://cribbnicolas.github.io/deltadictum/)**, with the benchmark on its [landing page](https://cribbnicolas.github.io/deltadictum/#measured). ## Install You need [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 22.16 or later and a git repository. **Claude Code**: ```text /plugin marketplace add CribbNicolas/deltadictum /plugin install dd@deltadictum ``` **Codex**: ```bash npm install -g deltadictum deltadictum install --host codex --project "" ``` Then open the project in Codex, trust it, and trust DD's hooks in `/hooks`. **OpenCode**: ```bash npm install -g deltadictum deltadictum install --host opencode --project "" ``` **Grok Build** (preview, not yet verified in a live session): `grok plugin install CribbNicolas/deltadictum --trust`. **Cursor** (preview, not yet verified in a live session): ```bash npm install -g deltadictum deltadictum install --host cursor --project "" ``` Then open the project in Cursor and trust the workspace: Cursor runs a project's hooks only in a trusted one. Then opt the project in from its root, and commit what it writes: ```bash npx deltadictum init git add .dd && git commit -m "Opt the project into DeltaDictum" ``` A project without a `.dd/` folder is left alone. [Getting started](https://cribbnicolas.github.io/deltadictum/getting-started) walks through each harness, the first memory and what you see at every step. ## Use Work as usual. When a fix teaches the agent something the code does not show, DD asks it to save a memory; you can ask for one too (`/dd:save`, or "save this as a trap"). Review what was saved with `/dd:review`, which opens a local review UI. `npx deltadictum doctor` tells you whether DD is working in the project. - [Using DD well](https://cribbnicolas.github.io/deltadictum/using-dd): what belongs in a memory, triggers that fire when they should, checks, the review UI, troubleshooting. - [Commands](https://cribbnicolas.github.io/deltadictum/commands): in the session, by harness, and the command line. - [How DD works](https://cribbnicolas.github.io/deltadictum/guide/how-it-works), [Memories](https://cribbnicolas.github.io/deltadictum/guide/memories), [Configuration](https://cribbnicolas.github.io/deltadictum/guide/configuration), [Storage](https://cribbnicolas.github.io/deltadictum/guide/storage), [Security boundary](https://cribbnicolas.github.io/deltadictum/guide/security) and the [behavioural contract](https://cribbnicolas.github.io/deltadictum/DD). The same pages are in [`docs/`](docs/); for language models, the site serves [llms.txt](https://cribbnicolas.github.io/deltadictum/llms.txt) and [llms-full.txt](https://cribbnicolas.github.io/deltadictum/llms-full.txt). Changes: [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md). Contributing: [CONTRIBUTING](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Next to `CLAUDE.md` Keep `CLAUDE.md` for what every session needs. DD is for knowledge that applies to specific files, commands or symbols: it is delivered at the action instead of at every session start, so a memory about one file costs nothing in the sessions that never touch it. `npx deltadictum import` turns the `.claude/rules/` and `.cursor/rules/` files that name paths into memories. ## Security and license The review UI listens on a loopback address only and answers only a browser holding the key it prints; proposals carrying credentials or unsafe content are refused ([Security boundary](https://cribbnicolas.github.io/deltadictum/guide/security)). Report vulnerabilities as described in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). DD is source-available under the [PolyForm Shield License 1.0.0](LICENSE), not an open-source license. You may install and use it for any purpose, including in paid work and inside a company, and you may change it and share copies with the license attached. You may not sell it, offer it as a hosted or managed service, or use it to provide any product that competes with DD. # DeltaDictum current contract

DD keeps project knowledge an agent cannot derive from the code, and delivers each piece at the action it
applies to. This page states what the code does today. Where this document and `src/` disagree, `src/` is what DD does and this document is
corrected.

## Memories

- A memory is one JSON file, `.dd/memories/<id>.json` (schema 8, `src/memory/schema.js`), committed with the
  project. Its kind is `decision`, `trap`, `failed_approach`, `fact` or `procedure`; its status is `candidate`,
  `active`, `contested`, `superseded` or `archived`.
- A memory carries a title, a body, `not_derivable` (why a capable agent reading the code would not work it
  out), triggers, an optional check, evidence and its origin (`model_initiated` or `user_explicit`).
  `not_derivable` is required for a memory to be live.
- At most one live (`active` or `contested`) memory per topic. A revision is a candidate that `replaces` a live
  memory; accepting it supersedes that memory in the same commit.
- Writes go through one journaled, locked transaction (`src/store/transactions.js`); an interrupted one is
  rolled forward before the next. Validation (schema, secrets, unsafe content, glob safety, sizes) runs before
  anything is written.
- An evidence file is hashed as text with CRLF line endings read as LF (`src/engine/file-hash.cjs`), so a
  checkout with CRLF and one with LF agree; a binary file is hashed as it is. A hash recorded from the raw
  bytes before still matches the file it was taken from.
- `.dd/local/` is derived and git-ignored: the compiled index, session files, telemetry, this machine's
  settings. `deltadictum
  compile` rebuilds the index; session start rebuilds a stale one.

## Delivery

- A memory fires when one of its trigger clauses matches an event: `on` names the event kinds (`prompt`,
  `read`, `edit`, `write`, `run`, `search`), and paths (globs with `*`, `**`, `?` and `{a,b}`), symbols,
  commands or prompt keywords narrow it. Matching is rule matching over the compiled index
  (`src/engine/match.cjs`), not similarity search.
- Delivery happens in the harness's hooks: at the prompt and before each tool call. Session start injects
  nothing into the agent's context; in Claude Code it shows the person one line (the hook's
  `systemMessage`, which the model does not see) with the number of live memories and how to open the
  review UI, except after a compaction. There is no MCP server. A shell command that only reads or searches (`cat`, `head`, `sed -n`,
  `rg`, `ls`…) is a read or search event, in Claude Code as in Codex; one that may change something (a
  redirection, an in-place `sed`, any other program) is a run (`src/hooks/events.cjs`).
- Each memory is delivered at most once per epoch of a session, and once per subagent (`src/engine/ledger.cjs`);
  a compaction or `/clear` starts a new epoch. The ledger's claim records the dimension that fired the
  memory (or `check`), the event kind and the time. A delivery is at most 10,000 characters (`delivery_limit`
  in `.dd/config.json`, 2,000 to 50,000, compiled into the index): what does not fit whole is named and
  arrives at its next event. Each delivery leaves a ledger line with its event, counts and size, never its
  content. Stale evidence and disputed memories are marked.
- Delivered text is advisory project knowledge. It never outranks the host, the user or the current code.
  Every delivery and every check report ends with a line saying so to the agent: apply it unless the user
  explicitly asked for what it rules out, and then do what the user asked and say which memory it departs
  from. The ledger's size counts the knowledge, not that line.

## Checks

- A memory may carry a declarative check: a regular expression over a changed file (`if_content`,
  `unless_content`) or over a command (`if_command`, `unless_command`). A check never executes code.
- Its `violates` and `passes` examples must behave as stated, or the compiler leaves it out. Unsafe patterns are
  refused, and evaluation runs under a time limit.
- `when: turn` (the default for files) runs at Stop over the final state of the files the turn changed;
  `when: edit` runs at the edit; command checks run at the command. Only a violation the change introduced is
  reported: one already in the last commit (turn checks) or in the file before the call (edit checks) is not.
  A violation is reported at most twice per file per epoch, and a check that fired on a file the agent then
  left unchanged is recorded as a suspected false alarm. A check judges the first 256 KB of a file, and a
  turn check only the files touched by the event kinds its `on` names. Check lines share the
  10,000-character field with the delivery: a line that does not fit waits for the next call, and a check
  that throws at Stop never costs the turn its capture request.

## Capture

- A project opts in with its `.dd/` folder: a committed `.dd/config.json`, or its first memory. Without
  it, hooks record nothing and ask nothing (`src/hooks/hook.cjs`). `deltadictum init` writes the
  opt-in (`.dd/config.json` with the project id, `.dd/.gitignore`, `.dd/memories/`) and compiles; the
  Codex installer writes the config too.
- Hooks record a footprint per session: paths, redacted commands, search patterns, identifiers and outcomes.
  Prompt text is not kept, except a short preview of a prompt detected as a user correction. A session's
  first prompt, before any tool call or Stop, is never a correction: there is nothing yet to correct. Past 4 MB
  (about 7,000 tool calls) a session's footprint takes no more tool calls or corrections, only Stop's own
  markers.
- At Stop, DD asks the agent for a memory only when the turn holds evidence (a failure followed by a fix, or a
  correction), once per evidence set.
- The agent saves knowledge by writing `.dd/inbox/<name>.json` (the `save` skill). DD ingests it in the same
  turn: it validates the proposal, suggests triggers from the session when none are given, refuses generic
  advice, and answers with the result. A proposal becomes a candidate, or an active memory when auto-accept
  applies. A proposal on a topic whose candidate is still pending replaces it; the replaced candidate is
  archived, never deleted. Every ingestion leaves one telemetry line with its outcome and reasons
  (`.dd/local/telemetry/inbox.jsonl`), never the content.
- Auto-accept (on by default; `.dd/config.json` `"auto_accept": false`, or the review UI's Settings panel, turns it off) activates a candidate only
  when DD verified its grounds itself (a repository file it hashed, or a correction it recorded that names the memory and follows something the agent did), every trigger is
  live, it has no check, and it neither duplicates nor revises a live memory. A reported success never counts.
- The agent's requests to archive, revise, re-verify, merge or delete memories wait for a person in the
  review UI, which carries one out only when the person applies it; archive, re-verify and delete may name
  up to 200 memories at once. Delete takes only memories that are no longer live (archived or superseded),
  so a live memory is archived first and its file kept until then. A proposal or request may name a
  `batch`; the review UI accepts or rejects a batch whole, each candidate under the same rules as alone (a
  refused one is reported, the rest proceed), then carries out its archive, merge and re-verify requests
  and, last, its deletions, leaving revise requests, and any that could do nothing, to the person.

## Maintenance and review

- Maintenance runs detached from session start at most once a day, unless this machine's `maintenance` setting
  or `DD_MAINTENANCE=0` turns that off (`deltadictum maintain` by hand): session
  files are rolled up into `.dd/local/telemetry.sqlite` and pruned after seven days, unused memories are
  retired, and the similarity index is refreshed.
- An active memory whose paths were touched in at least 20 sessions (`retire.after_sessions`) without it firing
  is archived. A memory a person reviewed is never retired this way, nor one a pending candidate revises.
  Archiving keeps the file.
- `deltadictum health` reports dead triggers, memories with no opportunity or none used despite it, hubs,
  triggers only on central paths, suspected false alarms and stale evidence; for each memory, its fires by
  the dimension that matched; the capture funnel (asks, corrections, proposals stored, activated or rejected,
  rejections by reason) and the last deliveries. `recall` and `status` read the store. `deltadictum doctor`
  reports whether DD is working in the project (Node version, the opt-in, a readable config, the compiled
  index and its freshness, session files recorded, the last maintenance run, and the counts that need a
  person: dead triggers, stale evidence, conflicts, candidates), as problems with a hint each or as notes,
  and exits 1 on a problem; a project that did not opt in is told so and nothing is created for it. The
  `review` skill shows its summary before opening the UI.
- `deltadictum ui` serves the review UI for one project on a loopback port, until interrupted: queues
  (among them the memories DD accepted on its own, until a person marks each as reviewed), a memory with its
  breadth, evidence, use and similar memories, a dry run of its triggers over recorded sessions, and every
  edit and status change, each validated as ingestion validates and followed by a recompile. It answers only
  its own Host, only a browser holding its key, and takes changes only as JSON.

## Harnesses

- Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode are supported: install, save, delivery and recall were verified in live
  sessions (Codex with codex-cli 0.163 and OpenCode 1.19.3, 2026-10-22). Codex receives the same delivery
  through its hooks: its shell tool is classified as Claude Code's Bash is, `apply_patch` headers name the
  edited files, and Stop answers with a block (`src/hooks/codex.cjs`). OpenCode receives memories appended
  to the tool result, leaving the system prompt and its cache alone, and its writes into the inbox are
  ingested in the same result (`adapters/opencode/index.js`). `deltadictum install --host codex|opencode`
  writes either project's configuration.
- Grok Build is in preview: it runs the same hooks with its own payload, mapped from its hook guide
  (`src/hooks/grok.cjs`), not yet checked against a recorded session.
- Cursor is in preview: `deltadictum install --host cursor` writes its project hooks (`.cursor/hooks.json`),
  which run with `--cursor`; DD reads Cursor's payload (`src/hooks/cursor.cjs`) and answers with
  `additional_context` before a tool call and at the prompt, never with a permission, and with a
  `followup_message` at Stop. A delivery stays within the 10,000 characters Cursor accepts. The shapes come
  from the Cursor CLI's source (2026.10.19), not yet from a recorded session.
- A hook that fails ends silently: DD never blocks the host.

## Import

- `deltadictum import [--from DIR] [--dry-run]` turns the project's `.claude/rules/*.md` (`paths` in the
  frontmatter) and `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` (`globs`) into active memories (`src/memory/import.js`): one
  `procedure` per file under `rules/<claude|cursor>/<file>`, firing on reads, edits and writes of the paths
  that match a repository file, the file itself as hashed evidence and as a revisit condition, accepted
  by the person who ran the import. A bare pattern (`*.ts`) applies across folders (`**/*.ts`). A rule
  with no paths or `alwaysApply: true`, one whose paths match nothing, and one whose topic a memory from
  elsewhere holds are skipped and reported. A body over 1,500 characters is cut at a paragraph and points
  at its file (`review.issues: imported_truncated`). A second import updates the memories whose file
  changed and leaves the rest alone.

## Limits

**DD is a plugin for coding-agent harnesses, not a service.** It follows that:

- Hooks are short-lived Node processes, and one runs before every tool call: matching is rules over a
  compiled index, never a search or a model.
- There is no resident process. DD runs in the hooks, in a daily detached maintenance run, and in the
  review UI a person starts.
- There is no runtime dependency and no model: Node 22.16 or later is all DD needs.
- Each harness's hook contract differs; its adapter translates events and output, nothing more.
- A hook failure never blocks the host.
- Everything is local: memories in git, everything derived in `.dd/local/`, no network request.

# Configuration

Every setting is changed in the review UI's Settings panel (the button at the foot of its sidebar), which
validates it, keeps every other key of the file as it is, and recompiles when the change needs it.
Editing the files by hand works too.

## The project: `.dd/config.json`

Committed with the repository, so the team shares it. Every key is optional, and the file's presence is
enough: a project with a `.dd/` folder (this file, or a first memory) is one DD records and asks in; one
without is left alone. `deltadictum init` writes it with the project id, beside `.dd/.gitignore` and
`.dd/memories/`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `auto_accept` | on | `false` (or `{ "enabled": false }`) sends every proposal to review instead of activating those backed by evidence DD verified |
| `delivery_limit` | 10000 | The cap of one delivery, in characters (2,000 to 50,000); what does not fit whole is named and arrives at its next event. By hand, run `deltadictum compile` after the change |
| `retire.after_sessions` | 20 | How many sessions must touch a memory's files without it firing before maintenance retires it (1 to 1,000). A memory a person reviewed is never retired this way |
| `project_id` | the folder's name | The label written into new memories; the memories already saved keep theirs |

For example, to review every proposal yourself:

```json
{ "auto_accept": false }
```

## This machine: `.dd/local/settings.json`

What one person turns on or off for themselves, never committed (`.dd/local/` is git-ignored).

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `maintenance` | on | `false`: session start no longer starts the daily maintenance run; `deltadictum maintain` runs it by hand |
| `record_payloads` | off | `true`: every hook appends what the harness sent it to `.dd/local/payloads.jsonl`, to check a harness against a real session. Turn it off when done; the file grows with every tool call |

Two environment variables do the same for one process, where no file can: `DD_MAINTENANCE=0` keeps CI and
DD's own tests from starting maintenance, and `DD_CAPTURE_PAYLOADS=<file>` records payloads into that file,
also in a project that has not opted in.

# How DD works

DD keeps knowledge an agent cannot derive from the code and delivers each piece at the action it applies
to. The behavioural contract is [`docs/DD.md`](../DD.md).

## The loop

![The DD loop: session start, prompt or tool call, deliver, check, stop, review, and back through git](../assets/dd-loop.svg)

The six boxes of the diagram, in order:

1. **Session start: compile the index.** DD compiles the project's memories into an index when they
   changed (`.dd/local/compiled/index.json`). Nothing enters the agent's context; in Claude Code you see one line
   with the number of live memories and how to open the review UI.
2. **Prompt or tool call: match the triggers.** At each prompt and before each tool call, a hook turns the
   event into its kind and paths (a read, an edit, a command…) and matches it against the triggers. In a
   project that opted in (a `.dd/` folder), it also records the session's footprint: paths, redacted
   commands, how they ended, your corrections.
3. **Deliver, once per session.** The memories that matched are added to the agent's context, once per
   session and subagent; a compaction or `/clear` re-arms them.
4. **Check edits and commands.** Commands and edits are checked against the rules memories carry; at the
   end of the turn, the files the turn changed are checked once in their final state.
5. **Stop: ask to save after a fix.** At the end of a turn that held a failure followed by a fix, or a
   correction from you, DD asks the agent to save what it learned. What it saves is validated at once.
6. **Review UI, or auto-accept.** A proposal whose evidence DD verified becomes active on its own; any
   other waits for a person in the review UI. Either way the memory is a file in `.dd/memories/`: committed
   to git, it reaches the next session, and every teammate's.

Outside the loop, once a day and detached, maintenance rolls the session files up into local counters,
prunes them after seven days and retires memories that never fire although their files keep being touched.

<!-- for: opencode -->

On OpenCode, step 3 happens after the tool call, and step 5 does not happen: see below.

<!-- /for -->

## What the agent receives

```text
DD - project knowledge (tests/store.test.js):
[TRAP] Close stores in t.after - A test that opens a store must close it in t.after: …
DD - advisory: knowledge, not an order. Apply it to the task; a problem it shows outside the task is reported, not fixed. If the user explicitly asked for what it rules out, do what the user asked and say which memory it departs from.
```

The last line closes every delivery and every check report: a memory is advice, and the request in front
of the agent outranks it.

A delivery is at most 10,000 characters by default (`delivery_limit` in
[Configuration](configuration.md)); a memory that does not fit is named and arrives at its next event.
Stale evidence and disputed memories are marked. A check that fails says so with the file:

```text
DD - check (Close stores in t.after): This test opens a store without closing it in t.after. (tests/a.test.js)
```

<!-- for: claude-code -->

Claude Code reports each tool call to the hooks with its kind and files, and a failure as its own event
(`PostToolUseFailure`), which is how DD knows a command failed.

<!-- /for -->

<!-- for: codex -->

Codex reads files through shell commands and edits through `apply_patch`. DD treats a shell command whose
every step only reads (`cat`, `head`, `sed -n`, `Get-Content`…) or searches (`rg`, `grep`, `git grep`,
`ls`…) as a read or a search of the files it names, and a patch as an edit of the files its headers name.
Any other command is a run. Stop's message reaches Codex as `decision: block` with the reason.

<!-- /for -->

<!-- for: opencode -->

OpenCode has no hook that adds context before a tool runs, and text added to the system prompt changes it
on every delivery, which invalidates the prompt cache. DD therefore appends the memories that fire at a
tool call to that call's result, framed as advisory project knowledge, once per session; the system prompt
is left alone. A memory arrives with the result of the call it applies to, not before it, and there is no
Stop hook: DD does not ask the agent to save at the end of a turn, and turn checks do not run. A memory the
agent writes into `.dd/inbox/` is ingested at once, and DD's answer joins the result of that write.

<!-- /for -->

<!-- for: grok -->

Grok Build runs the hooks Claude Code runs, with its own payload: DD reads its camelCase fields and its
tool names (`read_file`, `search_replace`, `run_terminal_command`, `grep`, `list_dir`) as its hook guide
documents them. Grok adds a hook's context after the tool call, as OpenCode does, and drops the context of
a prompt hook, so a memory that fires only on a prompt's words does not reach the agent. Grok Build is in
preview: no real Grok session has been recorded yet; the "Record hook payloads" setting
([Configuration](configuration.md#this-machine-ddlocalsettingsjson)) records one.

<!-- /for -->

<!-- for: cursor -->

Cursor runs the hooks `deltadictum install --host cursor` writes into `.cursor/hooks.json`, with its own
payload: DD reads `conversation_id` as the session and Cursor's tools (`Read`, `Write`, `Shell`, `Grep`,
`List`, `Delete`). Cursor makes every edit a `Write` of the whole file, so a `Write` to a file that exists is
an edit. Memories reach the agent before the call, through `preToolUse`'s `additional_context`, and at the
prompt through `beforeSubmitPrompt`'s; DD never answers a permission. Cursor drops a hook's context past
10,000 characters, so a delivery stays within that whatever `delivery_limit` says. A failed call arrives as
`postToolUseFailure`, and Stop's message as a `followup_message`, the turn's next message. Cursor is in
preview: these shapes were read from the Cursor CLI's source (2026.10.19), not yet from a recorded session;
the "Record hook payloads" setting records one.

<!-- /for -->

## Saving knowledge

The agent saves a memory by writing a JSON file into `.dd/inbox/` (the save command tells it how; on Codex
it must write it with `apply_patch`, since a file written by a shell redirect is not ingested). DD ingests
it in the same turn and answers:

- **stored as active**, when DD verified the evidence itself (a file it hashed, or a correction it
  recorded that names the memory and follows something the agent did), every trigger can fire, the memory
  has no check and duplicates nothing live (auto-accept, on by default);
- **stored as a candidate** for review, saying which condition was not met;
- **rejected** with reasons, for example generic advice, a missing `not_derivable` or a secret in the text.

When no trigger is given, DD suggests one from what the session touched. The agent can also ask to
archive, revise, re-verify, merge or delete memories; those requests, like what DD activated on its own,
wait in the [review UI](../using-dd.md#the-review-ui) for a person. Delete takes only memories already
archived or superseded.

# Memories

A memory is one JSON file, `.dd/memories/<id>.json`, committed with the project. The authoritative
definition is `src/memory/schema.js`.

```json
{
  "schema_version": 8,
  "id": "6f1c…",
  "project_id": "my-app",
  "topic": "testing/store-handle",
  "kind": "trap",
  "status": "active",
  "title": "Close stores in t.after",
  "body": "A test that opens a store must close it in t.after: a failing assertion otherwise leaves the handle open and node --test never ends.",
  "not_derivable": "Only a hung CI run shows it; no test or comment says so.",
  "triggers": [{ "on": ["edit", "write"], "paths": ["tests/**/*.test.js"], "symbols": ["createStore"] }],
  "evidence": [{ "type": "file", "path": "tests/store.test.js", "sha256": "…", "summary": "The test that hung" }],
  "origin": "model_initiated",
  "replaces": null,
  "revisit_when": [],
  "review": { "issues": [] },
  "created": "2026-10-13T12:00:00.000Z",
  "updated": "2026-10-13T12:00:00.000Z"
}
```

## Kinds

| Kind | For | Delivered as |
|---|---|---|
| `trap` | Something that breaks, and how to avoid it | `[TRAP]` |
| `decision` | A project choice, with why | `[DECISION]` |
| `failed_approach` | Something tried and abandoned | `[ABANDONED]` |
| `procedure` | Steps to follow for a recurring task | `[PROCEDURE]` |
| `fact` | A fact about the project or its environment the code does not show | `[FACT]` |

## Fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `topic` | `area/subject` path; at most one live memory per topic |
| `title`, `body` | What the agent reads: title up to 200 characters, body up to 1,500 |
| `not_derivable` | Why an agent reading the code, tests and docs would not work this out (up to 300 characters); required for a live memory |
| `triggers` | When DD delivers it (below) |
| `check` | An optional rule DD checks the agent's changes against (below) |
| `evidence` | `file` (a repository path DD hashes), `observation`, `correction` or `note`, each with a summary |
| `origin` | `model_initiated` (the agent decided) or `user_explicit` (a person asked or edited it) |
| `replaces` | The live memory a candidate revises; accepting it supersedes that one |
| `revisit_when` | Conditions under which the memory should be reviewed again |

## Triggers

A trigger clause names the events it applies to in `on`: `prompt`, `read`, `edit`, `write`, `search` or
`run`. At least one more field narrows it; fields in one clause must all match, and a memory fires when
any of its clauses matches.

| Field | Matches | Use for |
|---|---|---|
| `paths` | Repository files the event touches, as globs (`*`, `**`, `?`, `{a,b}`) | Knowledge about particular files or folders (most memories) |
| `symbols` | Identifiers in the edited or written text | A function or class, wherever it is used |
| `commands` | Words of a command the agent runs | Traps around `npm test`, `git push`, a script |
| `keywords` | Words or phrases of the prompt or tool call | Decisions a person is likely to ask about |
| `not`, `not_paths` | Phrases or globs that cancel the clause | Excluding fixtures, generated files, a subfolder |

`deltadictum health` and the review UI report triggers that can never fire (a glob with no file, a symbol
absent from the code) and globs so broad they match much of the repository. How to choose them:
[Triggers that fire when they should](../using-dd.md#triggers-that-fire-when-they-should).

## Checks

A check states a rule DD verifies itself, as regular expressions; it never runs code.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `on` | `edit`, `write` or `run` |
| `paths` | The files it applies to (edit and write) |
| `if_content`, `unless_content` | A violation when the changed file matches the first and not the second |
| `if_command`, `unless_command` | The same over a command |
| `when` | `turn` (the default for files: once, at the end of the turn, over the files' final state), `edit` or `run` |
| `say` | What the agent is told, up to 200 characters |
| `examples` | `violates` and `passes` samples, required: a check whose examples fail is left out of the index |

DD reports only violations the change introduced (one already in the last commit is not), at most twice
per file per epoch (a session until its next compaction or `/clear`). A memory with a check is never
auto-accepted: a person enables it in the review UI.

## Statuses

| Status | Delivered |
|---|---|
| `candidate` | No: waits for review |
| `active` | Yes |
| `contested` | Yes, marked `[DISPUTED]` |
| `superseded` | No: a revision replaced it |
| `archived` | No: retired, merged or archived by a person; restorable |

# Security boundary

DD protects a project's knowledge and its review from other accounts on the machine, from web pages and
from text that did not pass validation. It does not protect them from the agent itself, which runs as you
and can write `.dd/` directly: review is a check on what the agent proposes, not a lock against it.

## Review UI

`deltadictum ui` serves one project on a loopback address until it is stopped.

- It answers only requests whose `Host` is its own address, so a web page cannot reach it through DNS
  rebinding.
- It answers only a browser holding the key printed with its address, traded once for an `HttpOnly`,
  `SameSite=Strict` cookie.
- It accepts changes only as JSON, which a cross-site form cannot send.
- Its page runs only scripts carrying the page's nonce, and inserts every stored text as text, never as
  markup.

## Memories

- Every memory is validated before it is written or compiled: schema, sizes, safe repository-relative paths
  and globs, and no credential in a recognizable shape or unsafe content.
- Evidence paths cannot leave the repository, and no memory reaches another project.
- Delivered memories are framed as advisory project knowledge; they never outrank the host, the user or
  the current code.

## Checks

A check is two regular expressions and never runs code. Patterns that can backtrack catastrophically are
refused, and every evaluation runs under a time limit.

## Hooks and data

A hook that fails ends silently and never blocks the host. DD makes no network request; everything it
derives stays in `.dd/local/`, out of git.

# Storage

Everything DD keeps for a project lives in its `.dd/` folder.

| Path | In git | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| `.dd/memories/<id>.json` | Yes | The memories: the knowledge itself |
| `.dd/memories/manifest.json` | No | A count and hash of the memories, rebuilt when they change |
| `.dd/config.json` | Yes | Project settings ([Configuration](configuration.md)); its presence, or a first memory, opts the project in |
| `.dd/.gitignore` | Yes | Keeps the paths below out of git; DD writes it |
| `.dd/inbox/` | No | Proposals the agent writes; DD deletes each one it stores and keeps a rejected one for the agent to fix |
| `.dd/local/compiled/` | No | The compiled index and memory bodies, rebuilt when the memories change |
| `.dd/local/sessions/` | No | Per-session delivery ledgers and footprints, rolled up and pruned after seven days |
| `.dd/local/telemetry/` | No | Check outcomes and ingestion outcomes, one JSON line each, rolled up into the database below |
| `.dd/local/telemetry.sqlite` | No | Counters (fires by dimension, touches, capture signals, inbox outcomes), the similarity index and check outcomes, for health and retirement |
| `.dd/local/requests/` | No | The agent's requests waiting for a person in the review UI |
| `.dd/local/settings.json` | No | This machine's settings ([Configuration](configuration.md#this-machine-ddlocalsettingsjson)) |
| `.dd/local/payloads.jsonl` | No | What the harness sent each hook, while this machine records payloads |

Writes to `.dd/memories/` go through one journaled transaction (`.dd/.pending-write.json`, under
`.dd/.write-lock`), so an interrupted write is completed before the next one. Losing `.dd/local/` loses
history counters, never knowledge: the index is rebuilt from the memories.
